s0101.literal: Now my army is already numerous and the rebel band very few; we ought to divide the rebel army's strength and use the weak to master the strong—why gather their sharp edge and make them fight to the death against us?
s0101.idiomatic: Our host is already strong and the rebels few; we should split their forces and meet strength with weakness—why mass their keenest blades and drive them to die against us?

s0102.literal: " He then ordered the generals to disperse and post troops.
s0102.idiomatic: " With that he ordered his commanders to spread out and deploy their men.

s0103.literal: The rebels charged straight at Wang Sengzhi; Sengzhi drew back slightly. The Founder sent Xu Du leading two thousand crossbowmen to cut across their rear, and the rebels stumbled and broke.
s0103.idiomatic: The rebels drove straight at Wang Sengzhi, who gave ground a little. The Founder sent Xu Du with two thousand crossbowmen to strike their rear; the enemy faltered and routed.

s0104.literal: The Founder with Wang Lin, Du Kan, and others pressed them with iron cavalry at full strength; the rebels withdrew and held their stockade.
s0104.idiomatic: The Founder, Wang Lin, Du Kan, and the rest hurled their armored horse against the foe at full force; the rebels fell back behind their palisades.

s0105.literal: Jing's Bureau of Ceremonial Companion Lu Huilüe opened Shitou's north gate and came over in surrender.
s0105.idiomatic: Hou Jing's ceremonial companion Lu Huilüe opened the north gate of Stone City and surrendered.

s0106.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9. The sway-commanders Dai Mian and Cao Xuan and others stormed and took Guolin, one walled camp; the army again subdued four more walled camps.
s0106.idiomatic: See editorial note 9. The sway-commanders Dai Mian and Cao Xuan stormed and seized one orchard stronghold at Guolin, and the imperial troops took four more.

s0107.literal: The rebels returned and fought to the death, and completely recaptured the walled camps that had been taken.
s0107.idiomatic: The rebels came back fighting for their lives and clawed back every stockade and walled camp that had been won.

s0108.literal: The Founder was greatly angered and personally led the assault; soldiers vaulted the stockade and entered; the rebels again scattered and fled.
s0108.idiomatic: The Founder flew into a rage and led the assault himself; his men swarmed over the palisades, and the rebels broke and ran once more.

s0109.literal: Jing with a hundred-odd horsemen cast aside their halberds and took up blades, charging left and right through the battle line; the line did not break. Jing's troops were routed in great collapse; pursuit drove them north to Ximing Gate.
s0109.idiomatic: Hou Jing, with a little over a hundred riders, threw down his halberds, drew his blades, and charged back and forth through the ranks, but the line held. His army shattered; the pursuit chased them as far as the Western Bright Gate.

s0110.literal: Jing reached below the palace gate, dared not enter the terrace, sent trusted men to fetch his two sons, and fled.
s0110.idiomatic: Hou Jing came to the palace gate but dared not enter the terrace city; he sent trusted men to fetch his two sons and fled.

s0111.literal: The Founder led troops out to Guangling to meet contingencies; when Jing's general Guo Yuanjian fled to Qi, Editorial footnote marker 10. the Founder took in his following of three thousand men and returned.
s0111.idiomatic: The Founder marched out to Guangling to meet developments; when Hou Jing's general Guo Yuanjian defected to Northern Qi, See editorial note 10. the Founder enrolled his three-thousand-man command and returned.

s0112.literal: Sengbian memorialized that the Founder should garrison Jingkou.
s0112.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian urged that the Founder take post at Jingkou.

s0113.literal: In the fifth month, Qi sent Xin Shu to besiege Yan Chaoda at Qin commandery; the Founder ordered Xu Du to lead troops to help him hold firm.
s0113.idiomatic: In the fifth month Northern Qi sent Xin Shu to besiege Yan Chaoda in Qin commandery; the Founder ordered Xu Du to reinforce him and hold the city.

s0114.literal: Qi troops numbered seventy thousand; they filled the moat, raised earthen mountains, dug underground passages, and pressed the attack fiercely.
s0114.idiomatic: The Qi host numbered seventy thousand. They filled the ditches, heaped earthworks, sank saps, and pressed the siege without respite.

s0115.literal: The Founder himself led ten thousand men to relieve the siege, loosed troops to strike Qi from four sides, bows and crossbows flew in disorder; the Prince of Pingqin of Qi was struck by a flowing arrow and died; several hundred heads were cut; the Qi men gathered their army and withdrew.
s0115.idiomatic: The Founder led ten thousand men in person to break the encirclement and sent his troops against the Qi from all four quarters; arrows flew in clouds. The Prince of Pingqin of Qi took a stray shaft and died; several hundred heads were taken before the northerners drew off.

s0116.literal: The Founder marshaled his troops and returned south, sending Recorder-Attendant Staff Officer Liu Benren to present news of victory at Jiangling.
s0116.idiomatic: The Founder re-formed his columns and marched south, dispatching his recorder-attendant Liu Benren to Jiangling with news of victory.

s0117.literal: In the eleventh month, Western Wei captured Jiangling. The Founder with Wang Sengbian and others advanced a memorial from Jiang Province asking the Prince of Jin'an to exercise regency as Grand Steward, and also sent Chief Clerk Xie Zhe with a memorial urging him to ascend.
s0117.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Western Wei took Jiangling. The Founder and Wang Sengbian advanced a memorial from Jiang Province asking the Prince of Jin'an to rule as regent in the Grand Steward's name, and sent chief clerk Xie Zhe with a further memorial urging his accession.

s0118.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin'an arrived from Xunyang, entered and dwelt in the audience hall; the court granted the Founder a retinue of twenty halberd-bearers.
s0118.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin'an came up from Xunyang and took his seat in the audience hall; the court gave the Founder a guard of twenty sword-bearers.

s0119.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Qi sent back the Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming to restore the altars of state; Editorial footnote marker 13. Wang Sengbian received him; he took the throne and changed the era title to Tiancheng, making the Prince of Jin'an crown prince.
s0119.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Northern Qi returned the Marquis of Zhenyang, Shen Ming, to restore the dynasty; See editorial note 13. Wang Sengbian welcomed him. Shen Ming took the throne, changed the era name to Tiancheng, and made the Prince of Jin'an crown prince.

s0120.literal: Earlier, when Qi requested to restore Zhenyang, the Founder thought it could not be done and sent envoys to Sengbian arguing bitterly back and forth four times; Sengbian in the end would not follow.
s0120.idiomatic: When Qi had first asked to restore the Marquis of Zhenyang, the Founder had judged it ruinous and sent envoys to Wang Sengbian to argue the point back and forth four times; Sengbian would not be moved.

s0121.literal: The Founder was often angry and sighing in private, telling those close to him: "Emperor Wu, though of the clan firm as bedrock and spread far over the four seas—for quelling insult and revenge and crossing hardship, only Emperor Xiaoyuan suffices; his achievements flourish as no earlier age has heard.
s0121.idiomatic: The Founder brooded in private and often sighed to his intimates: "Emperor Wu of Liang was bedrock kin, his sway reaching the four seas—yet for wiping away shame and bearing the realm through calamity, none but Emperor Xiaoyuan can compare; his deeds tower as no age before has known.

s0122.literal: Wang and I were both entrusted with a weighty charge; the words had not ceased, the voices were still in the ear—who could have expected that suddenly there would be a different design?
s0122.idiomatic: Wang and I were both given a grave trust; the charge had scarcely faded from our ears—who dreamed that overnight he would turn another way?

s0123.literal: The heir is the High Founder's grandson, Prince Yuan's son; within the seas all eyes turn to him, the hearts of the realm dwell with him—what guilt had he that he was made to be deposed? To seek far among barbarians and set up one out of order—from this their intent can also be known.
s0123.idiomatic: The heir is the High Founder's grandson, son of Prince Yuan; the realm watches him, the people's hearts are his—what crime could justify casting him down? To go begging among barbarians and raise a man out of his turn—their purpose is plain enough.

s0124.literal: He then secretly prepared several thousand robes and brocades, gold and silver as materials for rewards.
s0124.idiomatic: He then quietly laid up thousands of robes, brocades, gold, and silver to serve as gifts for the troops.

s0125.literal: On the ninth month, renyin day, the Founder summoned Xu Du, Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, and others to plot; he then drew up the generals and soldiers, divided gold and silk, and advanced by land and water together.
s0125.idiomatic: On renyin day in the ninth month he called Xu Du, Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, and the rest to council, mustered his officers and men, shared out gold and silk, and moved by land and river alike.

s0126.literal: That night he set out from South Xuzhou to attack Wang Sengbian.
s0126.idiomatic: That night he marched from South Xuzhou against Wang Sengbian.

s0127.literal: On jiachen the Founder's infantry reached before Stone City; he sent braves over the wall from the north of the city.
s0127.idiomatic: On jiachen day his foot soldiers came up before Stone City and sent picked men over the northern wall.

s0128.literal: At that time Sengbian was just handling affairs; from outside came word that there were troops.
s0128.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian was still at his desk when a runner reported soldiers at the gates.

s0129.literal: Suddenly troops came out from within; Sengbian fled in haste, met his third son Yan en route, both went out of the gate together, attendants still several tens of men, fighting bitterly.
s0129.idiomatic: In a moment soldiers poured from within. Sengbian bolted, met his third son Yan on the way, and the two fled the gate together with a few dozen retainers who fought desperately to cover them.

s0130.literal: The Founder's great army soon arrived; Sengbian's few troops could not resist; he fled and climbed the south gate tower of the city; the Founder took advantage of the wind to set fire; Sengbian, cornered, was then captured.
s0130.idiomatic: The Founder's main force came up at once. Outnumbered, Sengbian ran to the south gate tower; the Founder sent fire on the wind. Trapped, Sengbian was taken.

s0131.literal: That night they strangled Sengbian and Yan.
s0131.idiomatic: That night father and son were strangled.

s0132.literal: At the eighth hour of midday, Editorial footnote marker 14. the Marquis of Zhenyang yielded the throne; the hundred officials presented a memorial to the Prince of Jin'an urging accession.
s0132.idiomatic: At the noon hour, See editorial note 14. the Marquis of Zhenyang abdicated, and the hundred officials memorialized the Prince of Jin'an to ascend.

s0133.literal: On the tenth month, jiyou, the Prince of Jin'an took the throne and changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Shaotai.
s0133.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the tenth month the Prince of Jin'an took the throne and changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Shaotai.

s0134.literal: On renzi an edict appointed the Founder Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Within and Without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Yang and South Xu provinces, bearing the staff, Minister of Works, halberd retinue, and pipes and drums as before.
s0134.idiomatic: On renzi day an edict made him Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief of all armies within and without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and inspector of Yang and South Xu, with the staff, the Ministry of Works, his sword-guard, and his pipes and drums unchanged.

s0135.literal: Again an edict granted the Founder a hundred suits of armor and arms; he might enter and leave the palace offices.
s0135.idiomatic: Another edict gave him a hundred suits of arms and license to ride in and out of the palace offices.

s0136.literal: Du Kan, Inspector of Zhenzhou, held Wuxing; he and Yixing Administrator Wei Zai together raised troops in revolt.
s0136.idiomatic: Du Kan, inspector of Zhenzhou, held Wuxing and rose with Wei Zai, administrator of Yixing.

s0137.literal: The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü to lead troops to attack Zai at Yixing; Kan sent his younger cousin from the same clan Beisou leading troops to oppose battle; Beisou was defeated and returned to Yixing.
s0137.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü against Wei Zai at Yixing. Du Kan sent his cousin Beisou to give battle; Beisou was beaten back into the city.

s0138.literal: On xinwei the Founder memorialized that he himself would campaign east, leaving Gaozhou Inspector Hou Andu and Shizhou Inspector Du Ling to guard the terrace offices overnight.
s0138.idiomatic: On xinwei day he memorialized that he would campaign east in person, leaving Hou Andu of Gaozhou and Du Ling of Shizhou to hold the capital offices.

s0139.literal: On jiaxu the army reached Yixing.
s0139.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the army reached Yixing.

s0140.literal: On jingzi they took its water stockade.
s0140.idiomatic: On jingzi day they stormed the river palisade.

s0141.literal: Qinzhou Inspector Xu Sihui held the city and entered Qi; he also invited South Yuzhou Inspector Ren Yue to raise troops together in response to Kan and Zai; the Qi people supplied their troops and grain.
s0141.idiomatic: Xu Sihui, inspector of Qinzhou, held the city and went over to Qi; he called on Ren Yue of South Yuzhou to rise with Du Kan and Wei Zai, and the northerners fed their armies.

s0142.literal: Sihui and others, because the capital was empty, led five thousand elite troops in a sudden rush to the palace gate; Hou Andu led five hundred fierce warriors out to fight; Sihui and others retreated and held Stone City.
s0142.idiomatic: Judging the capital bare, Sihui and his allies rushed five thousand picked men to the palace. Hou Andu met them with five hundred veterans; they fell back on Stone City.

s0143.literal: On dingchou Zai and Beisou came to surrender; the Founder comforted them and released them.
s0143.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wei Zai and Beisou surrendered; the Founder pardoned them and let them go.

s0144.literal: Because Sihui's bandits pressed close, he rolled up his armor and returned to the capital, ordering Zhou Wenyü to advance and attack Du Kan.
s0144.idiomatic: With Xu Sihui pressing the capital, he turned back at once and sent Zhou Wenyü against Du Kan.

s0145.literal: On the eleventh month, jimao, Qi sent five thousand troops crossing to occupy Gushu.
s0145.idiomatic: On jimao day in the eleventh month Qi sent five thousand men across the river to seize Gushu.

s0146.literal: The Founder ordered Hezhou Inspector Xu Du to build a stockade at Ye City Temple, south reaching the Huai shallows.
s0146.idiomatic: The Founder ordered Xu Du of Hezhou to throw up a camp at Ye City Temple, its southern face on the Huai flats.

s0147.literal: Qi also sent Anzhou Inspector Zhai Zichong, Chuzhou Inspector Liu Shirong, Editorial footnote marker 15. Huaizhou Inspector Liu Damo leading ten thousand troops; at Huye they crossed thirty thousand piculs of rice, a thousand horses, and entered Stone City.
s0147.idiomatic: Qi also sent Zhai Zichong of Anzhou, Liu Shirong of Chuzhou, See editorial note 15. and Liu Damo of Huaizhou with ten thousand men. At Huye they ferried over thirty thousand piculs of grain and a thousand horses into Stone City.

s0148.literal: On guimwei the Founder sent Hou Andu leading the navy in a night raid on Huye, burned more than a thousand Qi boats; Zhou Tiewu led naval forces cutting Qi transport; Editorial footnote marker 16. captured their North Xuzhou Inspector Zhang Lingzhou, obtained transport boats and rice numbering several thousand piculs.
s0148.idiomatic: On guimwei day the Founder sent Hou Andu's fleet to raid Huye by night and burned more than a thousand Qi ships. Zhou Tiewu cut their supply line on the water; See editorial note 16. Zhang Lingzhou, inspector of North Xuzhou, was taken, with grain barges by the thousand.

s0149.literal: He also sent Wei Zai to build a city at Dahuang, causing Du Ling to hold and guard it.
s0149.idiomatic: He set Wei Zai to build a fort at Great Ferry and left Du Ling to defend it.

s0150.literal: Qi men again south of Cang Gate water built two stockades to resist the imperial army.
s0150.idiomatic: The Qi built two more river camps south of Cang Gate to block the imperial troops.

s0151.literal: On jiachen Sihui and others attacked Ye City stockade; the Founder led iron cavalry and fine armor, coming out from Ximing Gate to strike them; the rebel army was routed in great collapse.
s0151.idiomatic: On jiachen day Sihui struck the Ye City camp. The Founder led armored horse out the Western Bright Gate; the rebel host broke in rout.

s0152.literal: Sihui left Liu Damo and others guarding the city, himself leading kin and trusted adherents toward South Province and Caishi; Editorial footnote marker 17. to meet Qi reinforcements.
s0152.idiomatic: Sihui left Liu Damo to hold the city and rode with his kin and sworn men toward Caishi in the south; See editorial note 17. there to welcome Qi reinforcements.

s0153.literal: On the twelfth month, guichou, the Founder sent Hou Andu leading naval forces to raid Sihui's family dependents at Qinzhou, capturing several hundred persons.
s0153.idiomatic: On guichou day in the twelfth month the Founder sent Hou Andu's ships to seize Xu Sihui's kin at Qinzhou—several hundred captives.

s0154.literal: The imperial army linked ships blocking the Huai mouth, cutting the rebels' water route.
s0154.idiomatic: The imperial fleet chained the Huai mouth and severed the rebels' river line.

s0155.literal: Earlier Venus from the eleventh month jingxu day had not been seen; on yimao it appeared in the east.
s0155.idiomatic: Venus had vanished since jingxu day in the eleventh month; on yimao it showed again in the east.

s0156.literal: On jingchen the Founder ordered all army units to deploy armored soldiers, facing Ye City establishing a floating bridge and crossing troops, attacking the two stockades south of the water.
s0156.idiomatic: On jingchen day he sent every command forward in armor, threw a pontoon opposite Ye City, and stormed the two camps on the south bank.

s0157.literal: Liu Damo and others crossed the Huai and set battle lines; the Founder supervised troops in fierce battle, set fire burning the stockades; smoke and dust filled the sky; the bandits collapsed; struggling for boats they crowded and pushed; drowned dead numbered in thousands.
s0157.idiomatic: Liu Damo crossed the Huai and formed line. The Founder drove the fight himself, torched the palisades until smoke blotted the sky, and broke the foe. Men clawed for boats; thousands drowned in the crush.

s0158.literal: At that time common people lined the Huai watching the battle; shouts shook heaven and earth.
s0158.idiomatic: Crowds lined the Huai to watch; their roar shook heaven and earth.

s0159.literal: The soldiers, taking victory, were all one against a hundred; they completely collected their boats and ships; the rebel army's spirit was cowed.
s0159.idiomatic: Drunk on victory, each man fought like ten; every enemy craft was taken, and the rebels' courage failed.

s0160.literal: That day Sihui, Yue, and others leading Qi troops by land and water, more than ten thousand, returned and held Stone City; the Founder sent troops to Jiangning to occupy strategic places and cut rebel roads.
s0160.idiomatic: That same day Sihui and Ren Yue brought back more than ten thousand Qi men by land and water to Stone City. The Founder sent troops to Jiangning to seize the passes and choke their roads.

s0161.literal: The rebels' land and water forces dared not advance, halted at Jiangning Pukou; the Founder sent Hou Andu leading the navy to attack and break them; Sihui and others riding a single boat escaped; they completely gathered military supplies and weapons.
s0161.idiomatic: The rebel columns dared not press on and camped at Jiangning Ford. Hou Andu shattered them on the water; Sihui fled in a single skiff while the Founder seized arms and stores beyond count.

s0162.literal: On jiwei the imperial army besieged the city from four sides from chen hour until you hour, took the small city on the northeast; at night they did not unbind weapons.
s0162.idiomatic: On jiwei day the imperial troops invested the city from dawn till dusk, took the northeast quarter, and slept under arms.

s0163.literal: On gengshen Damo sent envoys Hou Ziqin, Liu Shirong, and others to the Founder requesting peace; the Founder granted it; then outside the city gate they slaughtered victims for covenant; their generals, soldiers, and followers—nothing was asked; north and south as they pleased.
s0163.idiomatic: On gengshen day Liu Damo sent Hou Ziqin and Liu Shirong to sue for peace. The Founder agreed; victims were slain outside the gate to seal the pact. Officers and men went free to go north or south as they chose.

s0164.literal: On xinyou the Founder went out Stone City's south gate, displayed troops numbering tens of thousands, and sent the Qi men returning north.
s0164.idiomatic: On xinyou day he marched out the south gate of Stone City with tens of thousands in array and sent the northerners home.

s0165.literal: On renxu Qi Hezhou Chief Administrator Wuwanyuan from South Province fled back to Liyang.
s0165.idiomatic: On renxu day Wuwanyuan, chief clerk of Hezhou in Qi service, fled from the south back to Liyang.

s0166.literal: Jiangning Magistrate Chen Si and Palace Attendant Cadet Cao Lang held Gushu in revolt; the Founder ordered Hou Andu, Xu Du, and others to attack and pacify them; heads cut numbered several thousand; they were piled as a capital mound.
s0166.idiomatic: Chen Si, magistrate of Jiangning, and Cao Lang, a palace attendant, seized Gushu. Hou Andu and Xu Du crushed them; thousands of heads were heaped into a victory mound.

s0167.literal: Stone City, Caishi, and South Province were all pacified; captured horses, arms, boats, and rice were beyond counting.
s0167.idiomatic: Stone City, Caishi, and the southern posts were pacified; horses, arms, ships, and grain seized were beyond reckoning.

s0168.literal: That month Du Kan surrendered the city.
s0168.idiomatic: That month Du Kan yielded the city.

s0169.literal: On guimwei in the first month of the second year Du Kan was executed at Wuxing; Kan's cousin Beisou and Administrator of Soldiers Shen Xiaodun were also granted death.
s0169.idiomatic: On guimwei day in the first month of the second year Du Kan was put to death at Wuxing; Beisou and the army aide Shen Xiaodun were ordered to die with him.

s0170.literal: On gengshen in the second month the Founder sent Hou Andu and Zhou Tiewu leading war-boats to prepare Jiangzhou, then halting at Liangshan raised stockades.
s0170.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the second month he sent Hou Andu and Zhou Tiewu with the fleet to ready Jiangzhou and camp at Liangshan.

s0171.literal: On jiazi an edict said that when the Minister of Works had military affairs he might ride horses in and out within the city walls.
s0171.idiomatic: On jiazi day an edict allowed the Minister of Works to ride through the inner city whenever war called.

s0172.literal: On wuchen former Ningyuan Shicheng Duke outer-corps staff officer Wang Wei at Stone City's sand margin obtained jade seals with four knobs; the Founder memorialized sending them to the terrace.
s0172.idiomatic: On wuchen day Wang Wei, a staff officer of the former Duke of Shicheng, found four-knob jade seals on the Stone City flats; the Founder sent them up to the throne.

s0173.literal: On wuxu in the third month Qi sent naval Bureau of Ceremonial Companion Xiao Gui, Kutunfulian, Yaonanzong, Dongfanglao, Palace Attendant Pei Yingqi, Eastern Guangzhou Inspector Dugu Bie'e, Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang, Editorial footnote marker 18. supporting Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, and others, leading a hundred thousand troops out of Zhakou toward Liangshan; tent sway-commander Huang Cong struck in reverse, defeated them, and burned their front army's boats and ships; Qi halted the army defending Wuhu.
s0173.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the third month Qi sent Xiao Gui, Kutunfulian, Yaonanzong, Dongfanglao, Pei Yingqi, Dugu Bie'e, Li Xiguang, See editorial note 18. and the rest—with Ren Yue and Xu Sihui—at the head of a hundred thousand men from Zhakou toward Liangshan. Huang Cong, sway-commander of the inner guard, met them, broke them, and burned the vanguard fleet; Qi drew up at Wuhu.

s0174.literal: The Founder sent Dingzhou Inspector Shen Tai and Wu Commandery Administrator Pei Ji to join Hou Andu, together holding Liangshan to withstand them.
s0174.idiomatic: The Founder sent Shen Tai of Dingzhou and Pei Ji, administrator of Wu commandery, to join Hou Andu in holding Liangshan.

s0175.literal: From last winter until this time sweet dew repeatedly descended at Zhongshan, Meigang, Nanjian, and within Jingkou and Jiangning counties, sometimes three or four sheng, large as chess pieces; the Founder memorialized presenting it to the terrace.
s0175.idiomatic: From winter until now sweet dew had fallen again and again on Zhongshan, Meigang, Nanjian, and the districts of Jingkou and Jiangning—sometimes three or four pints at a time, beads as large as chessmen. The Founder sent it up as an omen.

s0176.literal: On dingsi in the fourth month the Founder went to Liangshan army to inspect.
s0176.idiomatic: On dingsi day in the fourth month he went to Liangshan to review the host.

s0177.literal: On jiashen in the fifth month Qi troops set out from Wuhu; on jingshen they reached Moling's old seat.
s0177.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month the Qi army left Wuhu; on jingshen it came to old Moling.

s0178.literal: The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü to encamp at Fangshan, Xu Du to halt at Mafu, and Du Ling to halt south of Dahuang.
s0178.idiomatic: The Founder posted Zhou Wenyü at Fangshan, Xu Du at Horse Pasture, and Du Ling south of Great Ferry.

s0179.literal: On jihai the Founder led the imperial clan kings and marquises and court ministers and generals outside the Grand Marshal gate at the White Beast stele to slaughter victims and report to heaven, Editorial footnote marker 19. because Qi men broke covenant, speaking impassioned words, tears streaming; the covenant allies all could not raise their eyes; soldiers watching were doubly roused.
s0179.idiomatic: On jihai day he led the imperial kin, nobles, ministers, and commanders to the White Beast Gate outside the Grand Marshal's offices, slew victims, and called heaven to witness—See editorial note 19.—that Qi had broken faith. His voice shook with wrath and tears; allies could not meet his gaze, and the ranks burned hotter to fight.

s0180.literal: On xinchou the Qi army at Moling's old county crossed the Huai, establishing a bridge stockade and drawing troops and horses across.
s0180.idiomatic: On xinchou day the Qi host at old Moling threw a bridge across the Huai and began ferrying horse and foot.

s0181.idiomatic: That night they came up to Fangshan.

s0182.literal: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, Xu Du, and others each led back to the capital.
s0182.idiomatic: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, Xu Du, and the rest pulled back into the capital.

s0183.literal: On guimao Qi troops from Fangshan advanced to Er'tang; roaming cavalry reached the terrace.
s0183.idiomatic: On guimao day the Qi columns moved from Fangshan to Er'tang; scouts brushed the palace walls.

s0184.literal: Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu halted at Baitu Ridge; flags and drums faced each other; the capital was shaken with terror.
s0184.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu stood at White Earth Ridge, banners within sight of the walls; the city quaked with fear.

s0185.literal: The Founder secretly withdrew three thousand elite soldiers and assigned them to Shen Tai, to cross the river and raid Qi mobile headquarters Zhao Yan
s0185.idiomatic: The Founder quietly stripped three thousand picked men for Shen Tai to ferry across the river and strike the Qi field headquarters of Zhao Yan

s0186.idiomatic: (Chen)—variant for the final character of Zhao Yanchen's name.

s0187.literal: Editorial footnote marker 20. at Guabu, obtaining over a hundred boats and ships and ten thousand hu of stored grain.
s0187.idiomatic: See editorial note 20. at Guabu, seizing more than a hundred vessels and ten thousand hu of grain in store.

s0188.literal: That day the Son of Heaven mustered the feathered forest forbidden troops, Editorial footnote marker 21. halting at Changle Temple.
s0188.idiomatic: That day the emperor called out the palace guard; See editorial note 21. they camped at Changle Temple.

s0189.literal: On jiachen in the sixth month Qi troops secretly reached Zhongshan Longwei.
s0189.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the sixth month the Qi army stole up to Dragon Tail on Bell Mountain.

s0190.literal: On dingwei they advanced to Mofu Mountain.
s0190.idiomatic: On dingwei day they pushed on to Mofu Mountain.

s0191.literal: The Founder sent Qian Ming leading naval forces out of Jiangcheng to intercept Qi grain transport, completely obtaining their boats and rice; the Qi army then greatly hungered and killed horses and donkeys to eat.
s0191.idiomatic: The Founder sent Qian Ming downriver from Jiangcheng to cut Qi supplies and took every grain boat; the northerners starved and butchered their horses and mules for meat.

s0192.literal: On gengxu the Qi army crossed Zhongshan; the Founder's army troops divided encampments at the east of Leyou Garden and north of Fuzhou Mountain, cutting their vital points.
s0192.idiomatic: On gengxu day the Qi crossed Bell Mountain. The Founder's men split camps east of Leyou Garden and north of Covering Ship Mountain, blocking the crossings.

s0193.literal: On renzi the Qi army reached northwest of Xuanwu Lake, south of Mofu Mountain, about to seize the north suburban altar.
s0193.idiomatic: On renzi day they came to the northwest of Xuanwu Lake, south of Mofu, aiming to take the northern suburban altar.

s0194.literal: Army troops moved from east of Fuzhou, encamping north of the suburban altar, facing Qi men opposite.
s0194.idiomatic: The imperial columns shifted east of Covering Ship and camped north of the suburban altar, line against line with the Qi.

s0195.literal: That night great rain, thunder, and lightning; violent wind uprooted trees; level ground water more than a zhang deep; the Qi army day and night sat and stood in mud, hung pots to cook; yet within the terrace and north of Chaogou the water receded, paths dry; the imperial army each got reliefs in turn.
s0195.idiomatic: That night thunder, cloudburst, and a wind that tore up trees left a foot of water on the flats. The Qi stood and slept in mire, cooking from pots slung on poles, while within the palace and north of Chaogou the ground dried; the defenders rotated fresh men.

s0196.literal: On jiayin there was a little clearing; the Founder ordered army troops to feed horses and take a bed-meal; at delayed dawn he attacked.
s0196.idiomatic: On jiayin day the sky briefly cleared. He ordered the men to feed their horses and take a meal in the saddle, then struck at first light.

s0197.literal: At yimao dawn the Founder personally led tent adherents out south of Mofu Mountain; Wu Mingche, Shen Tai, and others' army troops head and tail together raised; they loosed troops in great battle; Hou Andu from Baixia led troops cutting across behind them; the Qi army was routed in great collapse; cut and captured numbered several thousand; trampled and crushed dead were beyond counting; alive they seized Xu Sihui and his brother Sizong and beheaded them to display.
s0197.idiomatic: At yimao dawn he led his household guard south of Mofu; Wu Mingche and Shen Tai hit front and rear together; Hou Andu swept from Baixia around their back. The Qi host collapsed—thousands slain or taken, countless trodden dead. Xu Sihui and his brother Sizong were captured alive and beheaded as a warning.

s0198.literal: Pursuit of the flight reached Linyi.
s0198.idiomatic: The pursuit ran them down as far as Linyi.

s0199.literal: The armies at Jiangcheng, Sheshan, Zhongshan, and elsewhere in succession achieved victory; captured were Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and other generals altogether forty-six men.
s0199.idiomatic: Columns at Jiangcheng, Sheshan, Bell Mountain, and the rest won in turn. Among forty-six commanders taken were Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi.

s0200.literal: Their soldiers who could flee to the river tied reed rafts to cross; mid-river they drowned; floating corpses reached Jingkou; the water was obscured to the banks.
s0200.idiomatic: Those who reached the river lashed reed rafts and drowned midstream; corpses drifted to Jingkou until the water hid the banks.
